senses: to persist, endure or hold out
la:verb:obduro.html:
ob-dūro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.
Act., to harden, render hard (only postclass.); in the trop. signif.: obdurare se contra manifestam veritatem,: obdurata patientia,: obdurata nequitia,: obdurata verecundia,.—Esp., to harden the heart against God (eccl. Lat.): obdurare corda,; ; .—Pass.: ut non obduretur quis vestrum,.—
Neutr., to be hard or hardened; only trop., to hold out, persist, endure: pernegabo atque obdurabo,: persta, atque obdura,; : perfer et obdura,.— Impers. pass.: quare obduretur hoc triduum, * .
la:verb:obduro.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.

la:verb:obduresco.html:
ob-dūresco, rui, 3,
v. n., to grow or become hard, to harden (class. only in the trop. signif.; syn. occalesco).
Lit., : semen diuturnitate obdurescit,: nervis divinis,.—
Trop., to become hardened, insensible, obdurate: ita miser cubando in lecto hic expectando obdurui,: ad ista obduruimus,: usu obduruerat et percalluerat civitatis incredibilis patientia,: nisi obduruisset animus ad dolorem,: contra fortunam,; cf. : consuetudine,: amicorum alii obduruerunt,: Gorgonis vultu,at the sight of,: dociliora sunt ingenia, priusquam obduruerunt,.

la:verb:obduco.gloss: to lead, conduct, bring or draw towards, before, forward or against
senses: to lead, conduct, bring or draw towards, before, forward or against
to cover by drawing over; cover over, overlay, overspread, surround, envelop; heal; conceal
to close, shut up, bar; block
to draw in, drink down, swallow, down
la:verb:obduco.html:
ob-dūco, xi, ctum (
inf. perf. sync. obduxe, Arg. ad ), 3, v. a., to lead or draw before, lead or conduct against or towards, to draw or bring forward or around, draw over (class. and very freq.; syn.: obtendo, obtego).
Lit.: ad oppidum exercitum,: vim Gallicam obduc contra in acie, Att. ap. : Curium,: ab utroque latere collis transversam fossam obduxit, drew forward, drew, made, or extended a trench, : vela,: vestem, to draw on or over, ; : seram,to draw, close, fasten,: callum,to draw over,.—
Transf.
To cover by drawing over; to cover over, overspread, surround, envelop: trunci obducuntur libro, aut cortice,: operimento,; : vultus, of the sun,: caput,: semina cortice,: obducta cicatrix,a closed, healed scar,; : obductā nocte,overcast, cloudy, dark,; .—
To close, shut up (poet.): obducta penetralia Phoebi,: fores,. mors oculos coepit obducere, .—
To draw in, drink down, swallow: venenum,: potionem,: pultarium mulsi, to drink up, .—
To swallow up, overwhelm: uti eos, eum exercitum, eos hostes, eosque homines, urbes agrosque eorum ... obducatis (an imprecation to the gods below),.—
To contract, wrinkle, knit the brow: obductā solvatur fronte senectus,: frontem,: vultum,.—
To injure, harm (late Lat.): stomachum,.—
To bring home in opposition or rivalry to another: eum putat uxor sibi Obduxe scortum,.—
Trop.
To draw or spread over: obsidionem, Enn. ap. Paul. ex Müll. (Trag. v. 11 Vahl.): clarissimis rebus tenebras obducere,i. e. to darken, obscure,: paulatim tenebris sese obducentibus,.—
Transf.
To cover, conceal: obductus verbis dolor,: obductos rescindere luctus,: rei publicae obducere cicatricem,.—
Qs., to draw out, i. e. to pass, spend time: itaque obduxi posterum diem,.

la:verb:obducto.gloss: to lead or conduct in opposition or rivalry to another
senses: to lead or conduct in opposition or rivalry to another
la:verb:obducto.html:
obducto, āre, v. freq. a.
id.
,
to lead or conduct in opposition or rivalry to another: nec pol ego patiar ... measque in aedes sic scorta obductarier,; cf. obduco, I. B. 7.

la:verb:obdulcesco.html:
ob-dulcesco, dulcui, 3,
v. inch. n., to become sweet: obdulcesco, περιγλυκύνομαι, Gloss. Philox.: in earum familiaritate obdulcuisses mihi,.

la:verb:obdormio.html:
ob-dormĭo, īvi or ii, ītum, 4, v. n. and a.
, to fall asleep (class.): ebrium obdormivisse,: Endymion nescio quando in Latmo obdormivit,: sub taxo,: quem obdormire volumus,: Atiam obdormisse,: nepetam substernere obdormituris utile est, (Jan, eo dormituris).—
Esp., to fall asleep in death (eccl. Lat.): obdormivit in Domino,.—
Act. (anteclass.): omnem obdormivi crapulam,have slept off all my debauch,.
la:verb:obdormio.inflection: īvi or ii, ītum, 4, v. n. and a.

la:verb:obdormisco.html:
obdormisco, ĕre,
v. inch. n. [obdormio], to fall asleep (rare but class.): ibidem obdormiscemus,; : quid melius, quam in mediis vitae laboribus obdormiscere, * : in jure dicendo,: post cibum,: cantante eo,: testudines summā in aquā obdormiscere,.
